previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, and pacemaker was admitted for malaise, chills, and right thigh erythema concerning for cellulitis and possible sepsis. She was started on IV vancomycin and cefepime due to prior MRSA and Pseudomonas infections. Blood cultures, MRSA screen, and urine culture were negative, suggesting no bacteremia. Her symptoms improved rapidly, and antibiotics were transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. During the stay, she developed antibiotic-associated diarrhea, managed with loperamide and probiotics, and suffered a superficial perianal laceration from a fall on the commode, evaluated via sigmoidoscopy with no internal injury. Anticoagulation was temporarily adjusted due to subtherapeutic INR and the laceration. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, with warfarin dose increased to 3 mg daily, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up on INR.
